angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 785,445 km at 35.43 pc = 0.3 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 28.2210 +/- 0.0185 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 35.43 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.129 +/- 0.013 solar radii from DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract): 785,445 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.05 +/- 0.044 solar masses from DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6081 +/- 60 K from DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: DiTomasso et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 60779 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...97D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-60779.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.354, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
